overview:
Most Morocco tours show you the mountains through a car window. This eight-day private tour from Casablanca puts you on foot in them: two days of guided walking around Imlil, below Jebel Toubkal, the highest peak in North Africa, then a second, easier walk among the rock formations of the Dades valley. Between the walks comes the classic road to the Sahara: the Tizi n'Tichka pass, the ksar of Ait Ben Haddou, the Todra Gorge and a sunset camel ride into the dunes of Erg Chebbi for a night in a desert camp.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 8 days, 7 nights
• Start and finish: Casablanca (hotel or Mohammed V airport)
• Type: private tour with your own driver; certified mountain guide for the Atlas walks, local guides at Ait Ben Haddou and in the Dades
• Walking: an afternoon walk on Day 2 (2–3 hours), a full hiking day on Day 3 (5–6 hours), a canyon walk on Day 5 (about 3 hours)
• Highest point: a pass of around 2,300 m on Day 3; no summit climb
• Nights: Marrakech (2), a mountain guesthouse in Imlil (2), Ait Ben Haddou, Dades valley, desert camp in Erg Chebbi
• Activity level: moderate – good for walkers of average fitness

THE ROUTE DAY BY DAY
• Day 1 – Casablanca to Marrakech: about 240 km, 3 hours on the motorway.
• Day 2 – Marrakech to Imlil (65 km), afternoon walk to Aroumd.
• Day 3 – Full day hike through the valleys and villages around Imlil.
• Day 4 – Over the Tizi n'Tichka to Ait Ben Haddou: about 230 km.
• Day 5 – Ouarzazate, the Valley of Roses and a walk in the Dades: about 150 km.
• Day 6 – Todra Gorge and the dunes of Merzouga: about 300 km.
• Day 7 – The long road back to Marrakech: about 560 km.
• Day 8 – Marrakech to Casablanca: about 240 km.

WHY THIS ROUTE WORKS
Walking first, while you are fresh, and before the long desert drives, keeps the trip balanced. Two nights in the same guesthouse in Imlil mean you carry only a daypack: no packing and unpacking in the mountains. The Dades walk on Day 5 breaks up the road with real exercise, and the desert comes as the reward at the end.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Walkers and active travellers of average fitness, couples and friends who want more than a sightseeing tour, families with teenagers who like to hike, and anyone flying into Casablanca who wants both the mountains and the Sahara in one week.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you only want a taste of the mountains, take the [Imlil and Toubkal National Park day hike](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/imlil-toubkal-national-park-day-hike-from-marrakech/ec0e3b716bbad68797b6158b) from Marrakech. If you want to stand on the summit of Toubkal (4,167 m), ask us to add a two-day summit trek: it needs good fitness and is best from June to October.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Bring broken-in walking boots or trail shoes, a daypack, a water bottle, a fleece, a rain and wind jacket, a sun hat and sun cream. Mountain nights are cool all year and cold in winter. Your main luggage stays with the vehicle or at the guesthouse. Travel insurance that covers hiking is strongly recommended. Tell us about any knee, back or heart conditions so your guide can adapt the walks.
descriptions:
What to expect: an easy first day – a motorway drive south to Marrakech and a free afternoon in the medina.

Your driver meets you at your hotel in Casablanca or at Mohammed V airport. If you arrive in the morning, you can stop to see the Hassan II Mosque from its seafront esplanade before leaving the city; its minaret is one of the tallest in the world. The motorway then runs south through the wheat and farmland of the Chaouia plain, with the snow-capped High Atlas appearing on the horizon as you approach Marrakech.

After checking in to your riad, the afternoon and evening are free. Walk to Jemaa el-Fna square as the food stalls set up, explore the souks, or simply rest on the roof terrace before the walking days ahead. Your driver can recommend a restaurant for dinner.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
Morning – Pick-up at your Casablanca hotel or the airport.
09:30 – Optional photo stop at the Hassan II Mosque.
10:00 – Motorway to Marrakech (about 3 hours with a coffee stop).
13:30 – Arrival at your riad in Marrakech; free afternoon.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Guided visits inside the Hassan II Mosque run at fixed times; ask us if you would like to include one.
• Change money or use an ATM in Marrakech: you will need dirhams for the mountain and desert days.
• Check your boots and daypack tonight; anything missing can be bought in Marrakech.

INCLUDED: pick-up, private transport, bottled water, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: Marrakech (riad)
Meals: none (breakfast from Day 2)

What to expect: a short drive into the High Atlas, meeting your mountain guide and a first walk of 2–3 hours to a Berber village.

After breakfast you leave Marrakech and drive south across the Haouz plain to Asni, then up the Mizane valley to Imlil (about 1,740 m), the main trailhead for Toubkal National Park. The drive takes about 1.5 hours. In Imlil you meet your certified mountain guide, drop your bags at the guesthouse and have lunch on its terrace.

In the afternoon you set off on a first walk to warm up your legs: through walnut and apple orchards and along old irrigation channels to the village of Aroumd (about 1,900 m), built on a rocky spur facing the peaks. From above the village you look up the valley towards Toubkal. Your guide explains how Berber families farm these steep terraces and move their animals with the seasons. You return to Imlil by a different path for dinner at the guesthouse.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Departure from Marrakech.
10:30 – Arrival in Imlil, meet your mountain guide, settle in.
12:30 – Lunch at the guesthouse (not included).
14:00 – Walk to Aroumd and back (2–3 hours, about 300 m of ascent).
19:30 – Dinner at the guesthouse.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Paths are rocky and uneven; wear boots or trail shoes with a good grip.
• Mountain guesthouses are simple and warm, with hot showers and Berber cooking.
• Evenings are cool even in summer: bring a fleece.

INCLUDED: private transport, certified mountain guide, guesthouse with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: Imlil (mountain guesthouse)
Meals: breakfast, dinner

What to expect: the main hiking day – 5 to 6 hours on mountain paths, a pass of around 2,300 m and a picnic in the valley.

After an early breakfast you leave on foot from the guesthouse with your guide. The route climbs steadily on mule tracks through juniper and terraced fields to a pass of around 2,300 m, with wide views across to the Toubkal massif and down into the neighbouring valley. You then descend to a string of earth-built villages, where children wave from the rooftops and women carry fodder on their backs, and stop for a picnic lunch in the shade of walnut trees beside a stream. The afternoon brings you back to Imlil by a different path. Your guide chooses the exact route on the day according to the weather, the season and the pace of your group.

In many villages you can stop for mint tea in a family house, a simple and genuine moment of mountain hospitality.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Start of the hike from the guesthouse.
11:00 – Arrival at the pass; time for photos and a rest.
13:00 – Picnic lunch in the valley (included).
14:00 – Walk through the villages and back towards Imlil.
16:00 – Return to the guesthouse; free time.
19:30 – Dinner at the guesthouse.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Total ascent and descent are about 600–700 m each; walking poles help on the way down.
• Carry at least 1.5 litres of water, sun cream, a hat and a warm layer in your daypack.
• From December to March, snow can cover the higher paths; your guide then chooses a lower route.
• Tell your guide early if the pace is too fast: the route can always be shortened.

INCLUDED: certified mountain guide, picnic lunch, guesthouse with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: Imlil (mountain guesthouse)
Meals: breakfast, picnic lunch, dinner

What to expect: about 4.5 hours on the road with stops, over the highest pass in Morocco, and a guided visit to a UNESCO-listed ksar.

You leave the mountains of Imlil and drive back towards the main road over the High Atlas, climbing the Tizi n'Tichka pass (about 2,260 m) through Berber villages and walnut terraces. On the southern side the landscape changes completely: dry, mineral and red. You reach Ait Ben Haddou in the early afternoon.

With a local guide you cross the river and climb through the ksar, a fortified village of earthen houses on the old caravan route, used as a setting for films such as Gladiator. The walk up to the old granary at the top takes about 40 minutes and gives the best view over the Ounila valley. Stay for the late light, when the walls turn orange, before dinner at your hotel.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
09:00 – Departure from Imlil.
11:30 – Tizi n'Tichka pass (photo stop).
13:30 – Ait Ben Haddou; lunch (not included).
15:00 – Guided visit of the ksar (about 1.5 hours).
19:30 – Dinner at the hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Tichka road has many bends; take something for car sickness if needed.
• Snow can close the pass for a few hours in winter; your driver checks the roads before leaving.

INCLUDED: private transport, local guide in Ait Ben Haddou, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, entrance fees, tips.

Overnight: Ait Ben Haddou (hotel)
Meals: breakfast, dinner

What to expect: a morning along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs and an afternoon walk of about 3 hours among the red rock formations of the Dades.

After breakfast you drive to Ouarzazate, where you can visit the Taourirt kasbah or a film studio, then follow the oases east through Skoura and Kelaat M'Gouna, the town of the Valley of Roses, where hedges of Damask roses line the fields.

In the Dades valley, a local guide takes you on foot into the strange rock formations nicknamed the "monkey fingers": rounded red towers and narrow passages where the path squeezes between the walls, then up onto a ridge with views over the valley, its kasbahs and green fields. It is an easy, varied walk with a few short scrambles. You end the day at a hotel or kasbah in the valley.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Departure from Ait Ben Haddou.
09:15 – Ouarzazate: Taourirt kasbah or film studio (optional, about 1 hour).
11:30 – Skoura palm grove viewpoint.
12:30 – Kelaat M'Gouna and the Valley of Roses; lunch (not included).
14:30 – Walk among the Dades rock formations with a local guide (about 3 hours).
18:00 – Arrival at your hotel in the Dades valley.
19:30 – Dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The walk includes a few narrow passages and short steps on rock; good shoes are needed.
• In April and May the roses are in bloom and Kelaat M'Gouna holds its rose festival.

INCLUDED: private transport, local guide for the Dades walk, hotel with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, entrance fees, tips.

Overnight: Dades valley (hotel or kasbah)
Meals: breakfast, dinner

What to expect: a walk in the Todra Gorge in the morning, the road to the dunes, and a camel ride at sunset to a desert camp.

You drive up the Dades to Tinghir and its great palm grove, then into the Todra Gorge, where the canyon narrows to a corridor with walls up to 300 m high above a clear stream. Walk the flat path through the narrowest part. In the afternoon the road crosses the stony plain via Tinejdad and Erfoud, and the orange dunes of Erg Chebbi appear on the horizon.

At the edge of the dunes you leave your main luggage in the vehicle and meet your camel caravan. The ride takes about 1 to 1.5 hours, timed to reach a dune ridge for sunset. At the camp you are welcomed with mint tea, then dinner and Berber drumming around the fire under a sky full of stars. Tents have proper beds and blankets.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
08:30 – Departure from the Dades valley.
10:00 – Tinghir palm grove viewpoint and Todra Gorge walk (about 1 hour).
12:30 – Lunch near the gorge (not included).
13:30 – Drive via Tinejdad and Erfoud to Merzouga (about 3 hours).
17:00 – Camel ride into Erg Chebbi.
18:30 – Sunset on the dunes, then the camp.
20:00 – Dinner and music around the fire.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Pack a small bag for the night: warm layer, toiletries, charger, head torch.
• If you prefer not to ride, the camp can be reached by 4x4.

INCLUDED: private transport, camel ride, desert camp with dinner and breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, drinks, tips.

Overnight: Erg Chebbi (desert camp)
Meals: breakfast, dinner

What to expect: sunrise over the Sahara, then the longest drive of the trip, about 9 to 10 hours with regular stops.

Wake before dawn and climb a dune to watch the sunrise over the sand. After breakfast at the camp you return by camel or on foot to the edge of the dunes, shower at a partner hotel and start the drive back to Marrakech by a different road from the way out: through Rissani, the black stony desert around Alnif and N'Kob, and Ouarzazate, before crossing the Tizi n'Tichka one last time in the afternoon light. You arrive in Marrakech in the evening.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00–07:00 – Sunrise on the dunes.
07:30 – Breakfast at the camp; return to Merzouga, shower.
08:30 – Departure via Rissani.
11:30 – Alnif / N'Kob: coffee stop.
13:00 – Lunch on the way (not included).
15:00 – Ouarzazate area: short break.
16:30 – Tizi n'Tichka pass.
19:00–19:30 – Arrival at your riad in Marrakech.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Keep snacks, water and a charged phone in the car.
• You can ask for extra stops – an argan cooperative or a viewpoint on the Tichka.

INCLUDED: private transport, riad with breakfast.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, dinner, drinks, tips.

Overnight: Marrakech (riad)
Meals: breakfast

What to expect: a relaxed morning in Marrakech and a 3-hour drive back to Casablanca.

Enjoy a last breakfast on the riad terrace and, depending on your flight time, a final walk in the medina or a visit to the Majorelle Garden or the Bahia Palace. Your driver then takes you north on the motorway to Casablanca, to your hotel or directly to Mohammed V airport, which lies on the way into the city.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
Morning – Free time in Marrakech.
11:00 – Departure from Marrakech (flexible).
14:00 – Arrival at your hotel in Casablanca or at the airport.

GOOD TO KNOW
• For a flight from Casablanca, allow at least 3 hours between leaving Marrakech and check-in; for a morning flight, ask us to leave earlier or spend the last night in Casablanca.
• Exchange leftover dirhams before you fly: they cannot be changed outside Morocco.

INCLUDED: private transport, drop-off at your hotel or the airport.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: not included (end of the tour)
Meals: breakfast

faq.question: How fit do I need to be?
faq.answer: Average fitness is enough. The main hiking day lasts 5 to 6 hours with about 600–700 m of ascent on rocky mule paths; the other walks are 2 to 3 hours. If you walk regularly at home for a few hours, you will be fine. Your guide sets the pace for the group and can shorten any walk.

faq.question: Do we climb Toubkal?
faq.answer: No. The walks stay in the valleys and villages below Toubkal, with a highest point of around 2,300 m. If you want to reach the summit (4,167 m), we can add a two-day trek with a night in the mountain refuge; it requires good fitness and is best done from June to October.

faq.question: Is this a private tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Only your group travels with your own driver, and your mountain guide walks only with you. You can adapt the pace, the stops and the length of the walks.

faq.question: Who guides the hikes?
faq.answer: A certified mountain guide from the Imlil area leads the walks on Days 2 and 3: they know the paths, the weather and the villages, and speak English or French. A local guide leads the walk in the Dades valley on Day 5 and the visit to Ait Ben Haddou on Day 4.

faq.question: Do I have to carry my luggage on the trek?
faq.answer: No. You stay two nights in the same guesthouse in Imlil, so you only carry a daypack with water, snacks, a warm layer and a rain jacket. Your main luggage stays at the guesthouse or in the vehicle.

faq.question: What should I pack for the walking days?
faq.answer: Broken-in walking boots or trail shoes, a daypack, a 1.5-litre water bottle, a fleece, a light rain and wind jacket, a sun hat, sunglasses and sun cream. Walking poles are useful on the descents. For the desert night, add a warm layer and a head torch.

faq.question: What is the accommodation like?
faq.answer: Riads in Marrakech, a simple but comfortable family-run guesthouse in Imlil with hot showers, a hotel in Ait Ben Haddou, a hotel or kasbah in the Dades valley and a desert camp with real beds in Erg Chebbi. Standard and luxury options are available for the riads, hotels and camp.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Breakfast every day from Day 2, dinners in Imlil, Ait Ben Haddou, the Dades valley and the desert camp, and the picnic lunch on the main hiking day. Other lunches, the dinners in Marrakech and drinks are not included, so you can choose where to eat.

faq.question: When is the best time for this tour?
faq.answer: Spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November) are best for walking: mild days, green valleys in spring and clear skies in autumn. Summer is fine in the mountains but very hot in the desert in the afternoon. In winter the higher paths can be snowy and the guide uses lower routes; nights are cold in the mountains and the desert.

faq.question: Can we start or end at Casablanca airport?
faq.answer: Yes. Your driver can meet you at Mohammed V airport on Day 1 and drop you there on Day 8. For an early flight on the last day, we recommend leaving Marrakech earlier or spending the last night in Casablanca.

faq.question: Is the tour suitable for teenagers or older walkers?
faq.answer: Yes, for anyone who walks comfortably for a few hours. Teenagers usually love the mountain days and the camel ride. For older walkers, the guide adapts the pace and can shorten the main hike; tell us about any knee or heart conditions in advance.

faq.question: What if the weather is bad in the mountains?
faq.answer: Your guide checks the forecast each morning. In rain or snow the walk takes lower paths through the villages, or is shortened, and the time can be used for a cooking session or tea with a local family. Safety always comes first.

faq.question: Do I need travel insurance?
faq.answer: We strongly recommend travel insurance that covers hiking at moderate altitude, medical treatment and trip cancellation. The walks on this tour stay below 2,500 m and do not need any technical equipment.
